slides.title: Obfuscation
points: Obfuscation techniques reduce exposure of sensitive information by hiding, replacing, or disguising it.
Security+ Objective 1.4: explain the importance of using appropriate cryptographic solutions.

slides.title: Steganography
slides.teach: Hides data inside another file or medium so the existence of the hidden data is less obvious.

course.learn: Hides data inside another file or medium so the existence of the hidden data is less obvious.

breakdown.explanation: Message hidden in image, Data embedded in audio

course.why: It conceals the presence of information rather than merely encrypting its contents.
course.example: A message is embedded inside an image file.
course.check_q: What technique hides a message inside another medium?

slides.title: Tokenization
slides.teach: Replaces sensitive data with a non-sensitive token while the original value is stored separately and securely.

course.learn: Replaces sensitive data with a non-sensitive token while the original value is stored separately and securely.

breakdown.explanation: Replace the real sensitive value with a substitute token.

course.why: Applications can operate on tokens without repeatedly exposing the original sensitive value.
course.example: A payment system stores a token instead of the actual card number.
course.check_q: What technique replaces a sensitive value with a token?

slides.title: Data Masking
slides.teach: Obscures part or all of a sensitive value while preserving a usable representation.

course.learn: Obscures part or all of a sensitive value while preserving a usable representation.

breakdown.explanation: Hide the real value from view.

course.why: It reduces unnecessary exposure while still allowing users to recognize or work with data.
course.example: A support agent sees only the last four digits of a card number.
course.check_q: What technique shows only part of a sensitive value?

blocks.title: Hide, replace, or obscure?
items: The goal is to conceal that secret data is present at all.
Example: A message is embedded inside an image file.
The real sensitive value is replaced by a token.
Example: A payment system stores a token instead of the card number.
The value remains represented, but sensitive portions are hidden.
Example: Only the last four digits are shown.
blocks.example: Memory: Steganography hides · Tokenization replaces · Masking obscures.

questions.q: A secret message is hidden inside an image so observers may not realize the message exists. Which technique is this?
questions.explanation: Steganography hides the existence of secret data inside another medium.

questions.q: A payment processor stores a substitute value instead of the actual card number. Which technique is being used?
questions.explanation: Tokenization replaces sensitive data with a non-sensitive token.

questions.q: A help desk agent sees only the last four digits of a customer's account number. Which technique is this?
questions.explanation: Data masking obscures sensitive portions of a value.

questions.q: Which technique's main goal is to conceal that hidden data exists at all?
questions.explanation: Steganography conceals the presence of data inside another medium.

questions.q: Which technique is most appropriate when an application should use a substitute identifier instead of storing the original sensitive value?
questions.explanation: Tokenization replaces the sensitive value with a token.
